title: The pushed rotor and the Josephson junction

data.source: Numerical solution of ds/dt = tau + A sin(s), the RSJ junction equation, A = 1

prediction: Half turns at push 2 take 1.209200 and 2.418399; mean speed equals sqrt(push squared minus 1) at every push above 1; no cut at all below 1.
baseline: The textbook junction model (RSJ): voltage = sqrt(I squared minus Ic squared) above the critical current, zero below.
why: Every number agrees, because rule R4 with a cosine bump is the junction equation itself. CRR renames its parts and predicts nothing the textbook does not. One detail of the written prediction was wrong (one cut happens while a weakly pushed rotor settles); that was the checker's slip and both models agree on it.
